reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Progressive megalencephaly with somatic and often asymmetric (segmental) overgrowth and cutaneous capillary malformations, classically a midline facial or philtral stain
Neurological features include developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures, and a risk of cerebellar tonsillar herniation from the disproportionate brain growth
Connective tissue laxity, cutaneous syndactyly, polydactyly, and frontal bossing are supportive features
Part of the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum caused by post-zygotic (mosaic) activating PIK3CA variants
Because the variant is mosaic the condition is sporadic and not inherited, with the pattern of overgrowth reflecting the tissues carrying the variant
Brain imaging may show polymicrogyria, ventriculomegaly, cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, and white matter changes, so neuroimaging surveillance is important
Diagnosis often needs high-sensitivity sequencing of affected tissue because the mosaic variant may not be detectable in blood
reference.pathophysiology: Megalencephaly-capillary malformation syndrome is part of the PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum and results from post-zygotic mosaic activating variants in PIK3CA, which constitutively activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. Excessive signalling promotes unregulated growth and proliferation, producing brain overgrowth (megalencephaly with cortical malformation such as polymicrogyria), segmental somatic overgrowth, and vascular anomalies. Because the mutation is mosaic, disease burden and distribution depend on when and where the variant arose during development.
additionalDifferentials: CLOVES syndrome and other PIK3CA-related overgrowth phenotypes
Sotos syndrome and other macrocephalic overgrowth syndromes
additionalInvestigations: High-sensitivity sequencing of affected tissue for mosaic PIK3CA variants
Brain MRI to assess megalencephaly, polymicrogyria, ventriculomegaly, and cerebellar tonsillar ectopia
Serial head circumference measurement and neuroimaging surveillance for progressive changes
Echocardiography and evaluation for arrhythmia given reported cardiac associations
redFlags: Signs of raised intracranial pressure or symptomatic cerebellar tonsillar herniation
Cardiac arrhythmia or structural heart disease requiring assessment
reference.prognosis: Outcome is variable and largely determined by the severity of brain involvement, with many individuals having developmental delay, epilepsy, and a risk of hindbrain herniation requiring neurosurgical monitoring. Somatic overgrowth and vascular features are managed supportively, and targeted pathway inhibition is being explored for severe disease.
pitfalls: Excluding the diagnosis after normal blood testing rather than sequencing affected tissue
Overlooking evolving cerebellar tonsillar herniation on follow-up imaging
Attributing macrocephaly to benign familial causes and missing associated capillary malformation and overgrowth
Failing to recognise the sporadic mosaic nature and giving incorrect recurrence-risk counselling
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Consider targeted inhibition of the overactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway with an mTOR inhibitor such as sirolimus or a PI3K inhibitor as emerging disease-directed therapy
Undertake neuroimaging surveillance with neurosurgical decompression for cerebellar tonsillar herniation and management of hydrocephalus from disproportionate brain overgrowth
Control the associated epilepsy with antiseizure medication
Treat symptomatic or disfiguring capillary malformations with pulsed-dye laser
Provide developmental therapies and management of hypotonia and developmental delay
Arrange cardiac evaluation and monitoring for arrhythmia given reported cardiac associations
Reassure that the condition arises from a post-zygotic mosaic PIK3CA variant and is sporadic rather than inherited
Coordinate multidisciplinary clinical genetics, neurology and neurosurgery input
